title: Increment phase in a successor computation
statement: Let $k$ be a natural number, let $x$ be a Boolean input word, and choose one of the $k$ work tapes. Suppose configurations $a,z$ of the increment machine satisfy that running from $a$ for $t$ steps gives $z$, that $z$ is in the completed increment phase with flag $b$, and that no earlier configuration is in any completed increment phase. Starting from $a$ with the increment phase embedded into the successor machine's state space, the successor machine agrees through time $t$ with the increment machine, under the same state embedding. At time $t+1$, its configuration is $z$ with its state replaced by the exit phase if $b$ is true, and by the extension phase's initial state if $b$ is false.
hypotheses_covered: natural number $k$ and Boolean input word $x$
no earlier time below $t$ has a completed increment phase, for either flag
